title.narrative: Diocese of Isiolo Sustainable Livelihoods Programme

description.narrative:
The Catholic Diocese of Isiolo covers the entire area of Isiolo and Garbatulla districts and implements sustainable community development projects to help communities access essential services and reduce poverty. Over the last few decades, the Diocese through it's development office implemented integrated community development activities in micro-enterprise development, water and sanitation, agriculture and livestock development, education, community awareness and advocacy, human health and nutrition and disaster risk reduction.
As the number of disasters is on the rise, livelihoods especially in the arid and semi-arid areas have been adversely affected. Having just emerged from a drought period resulting from failure of six rain seasons, the food security and livelihood situation of majority of the people in the region has become fragile. This is compounded by outbreak of diseases such as cholera which claimed many lives in 2009. Malnutrition cases have also been on the increase. According to the Famine Early Warning System information, the larger Isiolo District will continue facing food insecurity.
There is need to develop and implement interventions that target not only the re-establishment of livelihoods but also measures that can reduce the impact of natural disasters such as drought on communities that have fragile livelihoods. CAFOD is funding livelihoods and disaster risk reduction projects in the Diocese. These projects complement each other.
The Sustainable Livelihoods project will be implemented in three divisions; namely Oldonyiro, Central and Sericho. A decision to implement livelihood activities in these divisions was arrived at through a process of needs assessment involving community opinion leaders. Needier locations and sub-locations such as Kipsing and Modogashe have been identified. Communities in these locations and sub-locations identified their needs as capacity building for community groups, improvement in animal and agricultural production, water and sanitation and access to financial services. The project will work with women and youth groups. The rationale behind this is that women are the ones who are affected most due to lack of water and the need to put food on the table. This will include women headed households. Youth groups will be targeted for support in economic activities as they are most affected by unemployment. Keen interest will be given to ensure persons living with HIV/AIDS as well as other special groups like the physically handicapped are involved in the project.
The project will target 4000 direct beneficiaries with 60% being women and 40% men and youth constituting 50%of the total number of beneficiaries. With this coverage the multiplier effect is expected to reach a total population of 10,000.
